text:
For an overnight pellet-smoker cook, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. Its 2,073.6Wh battery and 2,600W inverter give you plenty of startup headroom and, based on the cited estimate of 450–750Wh per 12-hour cook, capacity for roughly two or three cooks per charge. [Source and estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

For a lighter campsite setup, the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is a reasonable single-night option: it has 1,070Wh and a 1,500W AC output. [Comparison details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

Pellet grills usually draw only about 35–60W once running, but the igniter briefly needs much more. Check your grill’s startup rating, and keep in mind that lights or charging devices on the same station reduce runtime. This advice is for a **pellet grill/smoker**, not an electric smoker with a heating element, which needs far more power.
